title: EU AI toolbox groups standards, applications and prototypes
summary: How to read the EU public-sector AI toolbox: distinguish metadata, architecture, security probes, applications and prototypes before choosing a resource.

# EU AI toolbox groups standards, applications and prototypes


By OpenTools Team


·


November 7, 2026


Public‑sector teams can use the catalogue to find a starting resource. Its categories, licence labels and proof‑of‑concept entries require different follow‑up checks.


##


The catalogue brings together different kinds of starting point


The Interoperable Europe portal’s[November 4, 2026 announcement](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/interoperable-europe/news/ai-toolbox-support-public-administrations-adopting-ai) points public administrations to an AI toolbox containing standards and tools, use cases, training, and legal or procurement guidance. It supports the Commission’s Apply AI Strategy. The announcement is a current reason to inspect the repository; it does not make every listed resource a newly launched product.


The useful first distinction is what a resource actually is. A metadata specification, a reference architecture, a security-testing framework and a form-assistance application answer different questions. The portal’s[detailed tools page](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/ai-public-sector/ai-tools-and-solutions-public-services-copy) includes all of those, alongside explicitly labelled proofs of concept. Treating them as interchangeable deployment options would lose the distinction the catalogue itself supplies.


##


Match the resource class to the next decision


The following map uses the[portal’s descriptions](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/ai-public-sector/ai-tools-and-solutions-public-services-copy) . The final column is OpenTools analysis of the evidence a service team would still need; it is not a report that we tested the tools or verified their individual licences.


Scroll sideways to see all columns.


Starting question Listed resource and class What still needs checking


How should datasets and models be described consistently? DCAT-AP and MLDCAT-AP: metadata specification and application profile Exact version, required fields, local data rights and compatibility


How should a digital public service fit together? EIRA: reference architecture Local components, data flows and accountable owners; a blueprint is not a running service


How can a team look for LLM security failures? GARAK: security-probing framework Target version, relevant scenarios and actual observed results; catalogue inclusion supplies no test result


Is there a form-assistance application worth evaluating? OpenForm: conversational form completion, uploads and PDF generation Individual project terms, maintenance, hosting, accessibility and the proposed workflow


Is an experimental idea relevant? Objection management and Evaluation Bundesbot: explicit proofs of concept What was demonstrated and what remains unevaluated before production use


These categories help choose the next investigation. They do not rank the resources, establish that they can be combined, or show that any one of them meets a particular administration’s requirements.


##


Catalogue labels do not settle a project’s terms or compliance


The tools page labels DCAT-AP, MLDCAT-AP and EIRA as CC-BY 4.0, while its MLCroissant entry carries a CC BY-ND 4.0 label. Those are the catalogue’s labels, not an independent review of the terms attached to every code repository, dataset or document reached through an entry. We inspected the index, not each individual project’s current licence or deployment instructions.[Catalogue entries](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/ai-public-sector/ai-tools-and-solutions-public-services-copy)


The portal’s[legal notice](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/joinup/legal-notice) separately says hosted and federated projects and solutions are supplied by their owners under their indicated individual licences. It disclaims responsibility for those projects and says the portal’s general information is not professional or legal advice. The[introduction](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/collection/ai-public-sector/ai-toolbox-introduction) describes alignment with European principles and AI Act requirements; that description is not evidence that a specific installation has been assessed or approved.


##


Use a concrete service question to narrow the shortlist


OpenTools analysis: suppose an administration wants to help residents complete an application form. OpenForm’s catalogue description makes it a candidate for a closer look. DCAT-AP might help with a related metadata problem, but its presence in the same toolbox does not establish that it supplies the form assistant or integrates with that application. A security probe would answer another question again: what failures were found under the scenarios actually run.


A practical next record would name the service task, the selected resource and version, the evidence supporting its use, and the person responsible for accepting the result. For the form example, that could include a defined set of application cases and checks on accessibility, document handling and where data would be processed. These are proposed evaluation questions, not claims about facilities that OpenForm provides or tests OpenTools performed. Until the relevant project details and results are inspected, they remain unresolved.


##


Keep available catalogue material separate from future work


The November 4 announcement describes the Public Sector AI and Interoperability Readiness Pathway, or PAIR, as being developed. It does not establish a completion date or that every promised capability is available now. The toolbox is also described as continuing to develop. Those statements support using it as a changing discovery resource, with the selected entry and version recorded when a team makes a decision.[2](https://interoperable-europe.ec.europa.eu/interoperable-europe/news/ai-toolbox-support-public-administrations-adopting-ai)
